articles.title: Lawmaker reportedly loses leg as car ramming stuns Australia - NBC News
articles.summary: Lawmaker reportedly loses leg as car ramming stuns Australia  NBC NewsHelen Haines: Brendan Nugent silent and emotionless as he faces court over alleged attack on Australian MP  BBCAustralian democracy is usually peaceful. But there’s a homegrown history of political violence  The GuardianSuspect in vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker appears in court as police probe motive  ReutersNo bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Austra...
articles.full_text:
An Australian lawmaker was in critical but stable condition Tuesday after being hit by a car in what authorities said was a deliberate attack, shocking a nation where political violence is extremely rare.
Helen Haines, a 65-year-old independent member of Parliament, was struck Monday by a white Toyota Land Cruiser outside her electoral district office in Wangaratta, a town of about 30,000 people in the southern Australian state of Victoria. She underwent surgery overnight after being airlifted to a hospital in the state capital of Melbourne, about 150 miles away.
Local media reported that one of Haines’ legs had been amputated and that she was fighting to keep her other leg. The Alfred Hospital in Melbourne did not respond to an NBC News request for comment on the reports.
Australian lawmaker loses leg in car ramming attack
Police charged the driver, who they said was a 43-year-old local man, on Tuesday with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and causing harm to a federal official.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said earlier Tuesday that according to eyewitnesses, the driver had passed Haines and then did a U-turn, hitting her as she was standing by the trunk of her parked car.
“It’s clear that there was a deliberate act here. This wasn’t an accident, someone, you know, just skidding off the road,” he told the Australian Broadcasting Corp., adding that the motivation was not yet clear.
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told the network that witnesses had described seeing the driver reverse and then hit Haines a second time.
The suspect’s father said the family knew Haines well.
She was a “deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community,” Brendan Nugent’s father, Rod Nugent, and his partner, Christine Cunningham, said in a statement Tuesday.
“Helen has been our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable,” the statement added.
Political violence is extremely rare in Australia, where lawmakers are often out in public with little or no security and their accessibility is a point of national pride.
“It’s an Australian tradition to have a chat to a politician that you bump into at the shops,” Josh Roose, an associate professor of politics at Deakin University in Melbourne, told NBC News in an interview.
But threats are rising as political rhetoric becomes more extreme, officials and experts say, particularly since the Covid pandemic.
According to the Australian Federal Police, there were 1,067 incidents of threats, harassment, nuisance or offensive behavior against senior officeholders, parliamentarians and protected locations in the 2025-26 financial year, a 12% increase over the previous year and twice the number five years earlier.
In a 2023 study of Victoria state parliamentarians, 82% reported harassment and 85% reported threats of harm, said Josh Holloway, a senior lecturer in government at Flinders University in Adelaide, with female politicians more likely to face abuse.
Holloway said that Australian federal lawmakers, especially those in rural areas, typically work from “shopfront-style offices,” hold regular community meetings and attend local events without security.
Those practices may now come under scrutiny, “but reducing public access to their representatives can come with significant democratic cost,” he said in emailed comments.
Albanese said Tuesday that it was everyone’s responsibility to “turn the temperature down.”
“We can disagree with each other, but do it in a respectful way,” he told Australia’s “Today” show. “And that’s something that Helen Haines always was characterized by, was that respect that she showed to others right across the political spectrum.”
Albanese said later that he had spoken by phone with local barber Ricky Jefferies, who ran from his nearby shop to help detain Haines’ attacker in what Albanese said was “a great example of the Australian spirit.”
“I heard a loud bang, with no brakes. It was crazy,” Jefferies told reporters. “I just ran out the front to see what was happening.”
Jefferies, who said he removed a knife from the suspect’s pocket and pulled him out of the car, said a lot of people “just ran to help.”
Haines, a mother and grandmother who spent three decades working in rural health as a nurse and midwife and has a doctorate in childbirth, was first elected to Parliament in 2019, then re-elected in 2022 and 2025. Her family said in a statement that they were grateful for the “swift assistance of bystanders,” as well as first responders.
The increase in political threats in Australia follows a similar trend in the United States and other liberal democracies, Roose said.
“Australia always echoes what we’re seeing internationally, but sometimes slightly behind,” he said.
Since the pandemic, there has emerged a “level of extremist discourse that is unparalleled in Australian history,” Roose said, one that is highly influenced by politics in the U.S.
Australia, and particularly Victoria, had some of the strictest pandemic lockdowns in the world, which left residents feeling “imprisoned, but also disempowered,” he said.
Lingering feelings of resentment combined with the current high cost of housing, fuel and other necessities have contributed to a “deep hostility” toward the government, Roose said.
Politics in rural Australia, especially, have become “highly inflammatory,” he said, “because of the online space and the poverty and the desperation that, quite frankly, has seeped into these areas.”
Roose said the “paradox” was that the victim was Haines, who is not considered a polarizing figure and is “someone who’s grown up and spent most of their life in these regions.”
“It indicates, I suppose, the challenge facing democracies around the world,” he said.

articles.title: GREENVLOT and Cyberport Launch the Greenvlot Energy-Compute Asset Alliance, China's New Energy Going Global Enters a New Era of Collaboration - The Manila Times
articles.summary: GREENVLOT and Cyberport Launch the Greenvlot Energy-Compute Asset Alliance, China's New Energy Going Global Enters a New Era of Collaboration  The Manila Times
articles.full_text:
-- On October 15,2026, During the Future Industries Zone at the 2026 Hong Kong Electronics Fair (Autumn Edition) - a zone jointly organised by the Hong Kong Electronic Industries Association and the Hong Kong Trade Development Council - Sara Xiao, Chairman & CEO, GREENVLOT Group, spoke to the Hong Kong Economic Herald in an exclusive interview about how expanding AI computing power is reshaping global energy infrastructure, the path for Chinese new energy companies going global, and Hong Kong's role in global new energy and computing.
Centred on its intelligent new energy asset management platform, GREENVLOT has partnered with Cyberport to launch the Greenvlot Energy-Compute Asset Alliance (Green Energy Going Global Alliance). Built on industrial foundations with Hong Kong as its international pivot, the Alliance offers members three collaborative engines: finance, innovation and technology, and branding. Positioned as a collaboration platform for China's new energy industry moving from product exports to industrial collaborative expansion and asset deployment, it brings together Chinese industry players' capabilities for coordinated global expansion, to meet upgrading needs in global computing infrastructure.
AI Computing Expansion Reshapes the Energy Landscape as New Energy Moves from Generation Assets to Industrial Infrastructure
Rapid growth in the global AI industry is making power supply a core bottleneck for computing capacity deployment. Industry data shows that electricity consumption by data centres and digital infrastructure is rising sharply. A single AI data centre's load has risen from tens of megawatts (MW) to hundreds of MW, with some planned projects at gigawatt (GW) scale. By 2030, AI is expected to drive global data centre electricity demand up by more than 50%.
In Sara Xiao's view, competition in computing power is, in essence, becoming a competition in energy infrastructure. "What the global market truly lacks is not ordinary electricity, but stable, low-cost, low-carbon power of high quality that can be connected quickly," she said. New energy projects are shifting fundamentally in positioning - from conventional "generation assets" to "industrial infrastructure" supporting the digital economy. This brings new global expansion opportunities for China's new energy industry, which has advantages in production capacity and technology.
Breaking Traditional Industry Boundaries with a Full-Lifecycle Asset Management Platform
Unlike conventional equipment manufacturers or asset traders, GREENVLOT positions itself as an intelligent new energy asset management platform, building capabilities around the full asset lifecycle and forming an integrated closed loop of asset development, asset operations and AI solutions.
GREENVLOT operates a dual-platform model: its Shenzhen Qianhai platform leads project selection, development, construction and operations, providing the real-world asset base. Its Hong Kong platform at Cyberport focuses on R&D innovation, commercialisation and capital coordination.
According to the company, GREENVLOT has built a pipeline in Mainland China of approximately 7.6GWh of independent energy storage projects, including more than 4GWh of S-grade projects. In 2026, projects totalling 1.6GWh in Weifang and Weihai, Shandong Province, commenced construction in phases, providing solid real-world scenarios for technology and business model validation.
"We develop and build our own assets rather than simply trading them in the secondary market," Sara Xiao emphasised. "Real assets are the platform's core foundation. Although we operate as a platform, our underlying assets are real, tangible projects."
From Going It Alone to Going Global Together: An Alliance Model Tackling Industry Pain Points
Addressing the common difficulties Chinese new energy companies face going global, Sara Xiao said frankly that a single company going overseas can often only export products, while global competition has long since escalated into competition in overall organisational and collaborative capability. On this judgment, the Green Energy Going Global Alliance was initiated, integrating capabilities across the industry chain's upstream and downstream for coordinated overseas expansion.
According to the company, the Alliance brings together strengths in equipment manufacturing, technology R&D, engineering and construction, and financial services. Its members include leading equipment manufacturers such as HyperStrong, and technology companies in power conversion (PCS), energy management (EMS) and battery management (BMS).
Sara Xiao compared the Alliance to "a ship setting sail": "What the ship carries is the capability of the entire industry chain. Leveraging the boom in global computing power, and with energy storage as the foundation, we aim to bring China's supply chains and technologies to the world."
Financing is a common weak link for Chinese companies going global. Sara Xiao said that, drawing on the ecosystem advantages of Hong Kong, Singapore and other Asian financial centres, GREENVLOT can build sustainable financing structures for overseas projects - first addressing companies' immediate financing needs, then integrating resources to work with partners on overseas expansion.
Hong Kong as a Strategic Hub for R&D Innovation and Global Connectivity
For Sara Xiao, Hong Kong as the Alliance's starting point reflects a clear strategic logic. Beyond being an international financial centre, Hong Kong is a key node connecting global research, talent, capital and markets, offering irreplaceable value to new energy companies as a "super connector".
GREENVLOT has established an industry-university-research collaboration framework in Hong Kong, working with local universities and research institutes on long-term partnerships in storage dispatch optimisation, intelligent management and IoT data collection. Postdoctoral programmes and joint R&D platforms advance the commercialisation of research outcomes.
"Technologies already developed on the Mainland will undergo further R&D and refinement in Hong Kong before being commercialised in global markets," Sara Xiao explained.
Driven by the HKSAR Government's Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Development Blueprint and the Northern Metropolis development, a closed-loop industrial ecosystem is taking shape at an accelerating pace - linking R&D in Hetao, commercialisation in San Tin, manufacturing in the Greater Bay Area and global sales.
In Sara Xiao's view, Hong Kong, with a buyer network and international financial system spanning more than 140 countries and regions, can help Chinese new energy companies complete the critical leap from real-world validation to global expansion.
2027: A Key Milestone as the Collaborative Ecosystem Embraces the Global Market
On the industry outlook, Sara Xiao judged clearly: 2027 will see a concentrated release of global electricity demand and the peak shipping period for China's new energy manufacturing industry. As power supply capacity gradually keeps pace with computing capacity build-out, the computing industry is also expected to enter a phase of rapid global expansion in 2027.
"In this industry, there are no absolute competitors, only potential partners," Sara Xiao said, inviting global industry players to join the Alliance. Both established industry leaders and growth-stage technology companies can join, drawing on a shared pool of overseas projects and capital.
GREENVLOT was recognised at this exhibition as a "Star of Future Industries · Leading Enterprise" in the 2026 Future Industries Tech Top100, and its development path is also a microcosm of the upgrading of China's new energy industry: from exporting single products to exporting full industry-chain capabilities, and from single-company breakthroughs to building a collaborative ecosystem. Hong Kong is becoming a core strategic hub in the globalisation of China's new energy industry.

articles.title: Xinhua Headlines: "China Magnet" attracts growing interest from global talent - Belt and Road Portal
articles.summary: Xinhua Headlines: "China Magnet" attracts growing interest from global talent  Belt and Road Portal
articles.full_text:
A foreign tourist tries on hair ornaments at a mall in Shanghai, east China, May 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming)
* A growing number of foreign professionals are drawn to China by its expanding career opportunities, as the country's fast-growing industries strengthen its appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve global perceptions of China.
* China's emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice.
* As Chinese technology companies expand globally, their growing demand for international expertise is creating career opportunities beyond China's borders.
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- For 33-year-old Federico Flamenco, a Salvadoran engineer working in China's robotics industry, a once-distant career dream has become a reality.
"Working in robotics is something I could once only dream about. Now I work with robotic arms and get to see how quickly humanoid robots are developing here in China," he said.
After earning a bachelor's degree in El Salvador, Flamenco pursued a master's degree in electrical engineering in China. Currently at JAKA Robotics, a Chinese robotics company, he helps overseas customers find suitable robotic solutions, drawing on his engineering expertise and knowledge of Spanish, English, Chinese and Portuguese.
This undated photo shows Salvadoran engineer Federico Flamenco working at robotics company JAKA Robotics in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua)
Flamenco is among a growing number of foreign professionals drawn to China by expanding career opportunities, as its fast-growing industries strengthen the country's appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve perceptions of China abroad.
CHINA ON THE RADAR
Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of Direct HR, a recruitment firm that helps international companies in China hire senior executives, has seen the shift firsthand.
"Global interest in working in China has more than doubled this year compared with two years ago, with a major surge in inquiries in early summer," said Wickertsheim.
"We receive numerous inquiries from jobseekers in Europe, Australia, Arab countries, the United States and South America," she said, attributing the growing interest to a combination of "push and pull" factors.
In developed economies, sluggish growth and rising inflation have prompted more professionals to seek opportunities abroad, Wickertsheim explained. Layoffs at major technology companies have also driven skilled workers to explore other job markets, she added.
Meanwhile, professionals from countries such as those in South America admire China's rapid development and robust business ecosystem and hope to achieve joint growth with China, said Wickertsheim.
Wickertsheim noted that emerging industries such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and industrial automation are becoming increasingly important to her firm's recruitment business, while intelligent factories and robotic automation are emerging as key business areas.
Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of recruitment firm Direct HR, speaks about legal and HR updates for international companies in China at an event in Shanghai, east China, Feb. 25, 2026. (Xinhua)
Beyond career prospects, social media is also reshaping perceptions of China, Wickertsheim said. While Western media coverage of China has often focused on controversies, the country's 30-day visa-free entry policy has enhanced its appeal to foreign visitors, who share real, positive personal experiences online, she said.
"People saw China's safe, clean, modern environment, friendly locals and delicious food," she said, adding that these positive impressions have become another key factor drawing international talent to the country.
PULL OF INNOVATION
China's fast-growing emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice.
Cao Jun, chief financial officer of Hydrexia, a Chinese hydrogen energy company, said a major strength of Chinese technology enterprises lies in their ability to closely integrate technological innovation, product manufacturing and practical applications.
In the hydrogen energy sector, China's relatively complete industrial chain and strong engineering and manufacturing capabilities allow international professionals to participate in every stage, from research and development to manufacturing and commercialization in overseas markets, Cao said.
China's push for innovation-driven growth extends across its economy. In the first half of 2026, the country's GDP grew 4.7 percent year-on-year, with new growth drivers, including high-end manufacturing, the digital economy and modern services, contributing more than 40 percent to economic growth, official data showed.
China last week issued guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, calling for measures like closer integration of technological and industrial innovation and improved talent development mechanisms.
Such industrial policies also offer clues to where China's economy is headed. "The best industry development reference for foreign businesses and jobseekers comes from China's five-year development plans, which outline the country's investment priorities and emerging track directions," Wickertsheim said.
"More global enterprise executives and board members are now proactively learning about China's industrial policies, unlike in the past," she said. "This improved understanding helps foreign companies formulate more scientific China market strategies."
Hamza Boukili (L), founder of Shanghai Yunsuan Tech Company, talks to young entrepreneurs during the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai, east China, July 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang)
OPPORTUNITIES BEYOND BORDERS
As Chinese technology companies expand globally, their growing demand for international expertise is creating career opportunities beyond China's borders.
Hydrexia has expanded into overseas markets including the United States, Australia and Southeast Asia, building international teams that bring together employees familiar with Chinese technology and manufacturing as well as those with expertise in local markets.
Cao said the company aims to develop overseas teams that can serve local customers over the long term and become part of local hydrogen energy industries, rather than merely act as sales outlets for Chinese products.
Hydrexia employs about 250 people worldwide, with overseas business teams accounting for around 10 percent of its workforce. It plans to strengthen overseas teams over the next two to three years.
By the end of 2025, Chinese investors had established more than 50,000 overseas enterprises across 190 countries and regions, with China's cumulative outbound investment ranking among the world's top three for nine consecutive years. Chinese companies operating abroad have created an average of over 2 million jobs annually, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for improving support services for enterprises operating overseas and encouraging eligible companies to carry out mutually beneficial overseas investment cooperation.
Wickertsheim said Direct HR has received increased inquiries from Chinese companies planning to expand overseas. She expects Chinese multinational enterprises to generate substantial demand for overseas recruitment over the next five years.

articles.full_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian companies secured RM453 million in export deals at Semicon West 2026 in San Francisco, marking the highest value recorded under the Malaysia External Trade Development Corp's (Matrade) coordinated participation at the semiconductor exhibition since 2007.
The achievement involved 10 Malaysian companies, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), which showcased their capabilities at the trade event.
The export deals reflect international demand for Malaysian electronics and semiconductor solutions.
These products and technologies position Malaysian companies to tap opportunities arising from artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things, advanced technologies and industrial automation.
Matrade also strengthened industry ties through meetings with Semi, a semiconductor industry organisation representing 4,000 member companies, and the Phoenix Mayor's office to explore opportunities for greater collaboration and Malaysian participation in the global microelectronics and semiconductor ecosystem.
What To Read Next
A networking session facilitated by Global Chamber, an industry network organisation based in Phoenix, Arizona, also enabled Malaysian companies to present their capabilities, engage potential clients and establish new business connections.
Matrade chief executive officer Datuk Indera Abu Bakar Yusof said the participation was part of the agency's broader efforts to accelerate Malaysia's semiconductor exports, particularly among homegrown SMEs, deepen trade and industry linkages with North America and expand into markets such as Latin America, Central Asia and Africa.
"These efforts support the aspirations of the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the National Semiconductor Strategy, particularly in advancing Malaysian companies towards higher value-added activities, strengthening domestic supply-chain capabilities and capturing opportunities in the evolving global electronics and semiconductor industry," he added.
Matrade said it would continue to help Malaysian exporters strengthen their international readiness, build strategic partnerships and improve their competitiveness amid geopolitical uncertainties, intensifying global competition and rising environmental and sustainability requirements.
Through targeted trade promotion and industry engagements, the agency aims to help Malaysian companies move up the global value chain and support the sustainable growth of the country's electronics and semiconductor industry.

articles.title: Chinese travel firms' overseas boom comes with a cross-border payments catch - China Travel News
articles.summary: Chinese travel firms' overseas boom comes with a cross-border payments catch  China Travel News
articles.full_text:
“Our overseas business volume surged 30%, with significant growth in revenue, bookings and the number of travelers.”
An executive at one of China’s first major travel companies to expand overseas said the business had benefited from longer holiday periods, which drove a sharp increase in outbound bookings. Even some niche overseas destinations that once required Chinese travelers to make long, arduous journeys were now packed with visitors.
Yet despite the strong performance, the executive admitted with a wry smile: “We’re making money, but we’re also taking heavy losses.”
Why?
Because many Chinese travel companies expanding overseas are falling into the same trap: cross-border payments.
“Purchasing travel resources overseas requires substantial foreign currency reserves. But with exchange rates moving in our favor this year, our costs for buying hotel rooms, ground services and transportation overseas have fallen. The same amount of renminbi can now buy more resources when converted into US dollars,” the executive explained.
On the surface, Chinese travel companies expanding overseas seem to be winning on all fronts. So how can they still suffer significant losses?
The answer lies in a defining characteristic of travel consumption: the time lag between payment and fulfillment.
The length of this gap varies significantly by product type:
* For conventional outbound group tours, the gap between payment and fulfillment can extend to 6–12 months.
* For high-end customized outbound trips, it typically ranges from 90 to 120 days.
* For premium sports travel packages, the gap can be even longer, stretching from 2 to 18 months.
In other words, travel companies can face a gap of several months to nearly two years between receiving customer payments and fulfilling bookings.
Meanwhile, these companies often need to pay upfront to secure overseas resources, including hotel rooms, ground services, tickets and transportation. This requires them to convert currencies in advance and maintain substantial reserves of US dollars or other local currencies overseas.
That is where the problem begins.
The value of these foreign currency holdings is not fixed. Exchange rates fluctuate constantly, exposing travel companies to foreign exchange risk.
One Chinese travel company reported strong business growth in the first half of this year, yet foreign exchange losses reportedly eroded an amount equivalent to 80% of its net profit.
Beyond currency risks, cross-border payment operations present another challenge. Executives at Chinese travel companies expanding overseas also report that manual reconciliation, payment delays, repetitive processes and disconnected data systems are all too common.
To address these challenges, Chinese travel companies need to modernize their cross-border payment systems. One key step is to match incoming and outgoing payment currencies wherever possible, reducing unnecessary currency conversions and exposure to exchange rate fluctuations. Companies can also use more flexible payment arrangements and foreign exchange hedging tools to better manage currency risks and cash flow.
Another priority is to simplify payments to overseas suppliers. Multi-currency accounts, virtual cards and integrated payment platforms can help companies automate payments and reconciliation, reduce manual processes and improve visibility into their global financial operations.
Hong Kong-based travel group Travel Expert offers a practical example. With support from Airwallex, the company now enables customers in 25 countries to make online payments, while different departments use their own multi-currency virtual cards for spending and reconciliation. The company has reportedly reduced foreign exchange costs on overseas hotel payments by up to 3%.
As Chinese travel companies expand globally, competition is shifting beyond booking volumes and market reach toward operational efficiency and profitability. The next stage of international growth will depend not only on attracting more travelers, but also on managing cross-border payments more effectively and protecting profit margins.

articles.title: HKSAR eyes role in regional supply chains - chinadailyhk
articles.summary: HKSAR eyes role in regional supply chains  chinadailyhk
articles.full_text:
APEC meeting offers chance to deepen economic cooperation and services
The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministerial Meeting, which began in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on Tuesday, offers a platform for strengthening economic cooperation among member economies, economists told China Daily.
With the Hong Kong SAR and most Association of Southeast Asian Nations economies being APEC members, they can utilize this opportunity to discuss ways to step up economic cooperation, experts added.
For example, Hong Kong can play an important role in supporting the supply-chain restructuring process within the 11-member ASEAN grouping by providing a host of professional services.
READ MORE: HK, ASEAN can ‘drive economic cooperation across APEC’
Citing Asia’s strong interregional trade backed by market diversification and deeper trade ties, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects that Asia will contribute two-thirds of global economic growth in the next few years.
ASEAN economies, in particular, have benefited from a technology boom and strong growth in exports of semiconductors and an artificial intelligence infrastructure.
“The rise of technology has provided a sizable boost to several major Asian economies, with export growth having risen sharply in the first half of this year,” said Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF’s Asia and Pacific Department. He added that this was driven by technology products, strong demand for AI infrastructure, and investment in data centers.
Asia’s export strength extends beyond the technology boom, with trade — including nontechnology exports — performing better than expected despite tariffs. This was supported by the diversification of export markets, robust intraregional trade, and more trade agreements.
“Growth, surprisingly, has been stronger in India, while South Korea and some ASEAN economies have seen significant growth on the back of the technology boom,” Srinivasan said.
New calling
Besides strong exports, supply-chain restructuring serves as another driver of economic transformation in ASEAN economies.
To diversify risk and reduce dependency, many companies have adopted the “China Plus One” strategy, maintaining operations in China while establishing production or sourcing capacity in at least one other economy.
However, as this strategy becomes less effective amid widespread tariffs imposed by the United States, many companies are shifting to hedging strategies, localizing production and exploring domestic markets. During this process, they are seeing increasing demand for professional services to facilitate supply-chain restructuring.
Tang Hei-wai, associate vice-president (global) and director at the University of Hong Kong’s Asia Global Institute, said Southeast Asia had benefited greatly from the signing of trade pacts under the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership — a massive free trade agreement established by 15 Asia-Pacific economies, including 10 ASEAN members — robust infrastructure, and openness to foreign direct investment.
He said that Hong Kong, as a financial and professional services hub, can support ASEAN economies in restructuring their supply chains through trade finance and insurance.
Once Hong Kong successfully accedes to the RCEP, “it can help some of the grouping’s economies overcome challenges in supply-chain restructuring, especially when it comes to financial support and offering professional services, such as insurance, and supply-chain management,” Tang told China Daily.
ALSO READ: APEC economies urged to deepen cooperation
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said that besides ASEAN, Middle Eastern and Central Asian countries can also leverage Hong Kong’s professional services to promote economic growth.
“As Middle Eastern and Central Asian economies continue to develop and diversify, the SAR can support their economic growth by mobilizing long-term capital, broadening currency options, and managing and sharing risks,” Chan said.
He said international multilateral organizations, financial institutions and insurers can cooperate by using innovative methods to promote more efficient capital mobilization and risk management.
“With Hong Kong’s concentration of relevant professional expertise, abundant capital and extensive experience, the city can help structure projects to make them bankable, fostering a virtuous cycle in driving growth and investment opportunities,” Chan said.
Contact the writers at oswald@chinadailyhk.com

articles.title: Bangkok to Host 2nd Russian-Thai Investment Forum to Propel Bilateral Trade and Economic Ties - Nation Thailand
articles.summary: Bangkok to Host 2nd Russian-Thai Investment Forum to Propel Bilateral Trade and Economic Ties  Nation Thailand
articles.full_text:
Top business leaders, policymakers, and cultural figures will convene in Bangkok to strengthen trade, innovation, and strategic partnerships.
Senior officials, business leaders and development institutions from Russia and Thailand will gather in Bangkok from 29 to 31 October for the second Russian-Thai Investment Forum (RTIF), aimed at widening trade and attracting investment between the two countries.
Organised by the Russian-Thai Business Council (RTBC), the annual forum is themed "Russia-Thailand: A New Era of Economic Partnership".
It seeks to open up untapped markets, expand trade flows and speed up investment in key growth sectors. Core industries and the new economy The business programme covers both traditional economic pillars and emerging trends.
The first day, "Drivers of Core Industries", will focus on foundational sectors, including metallurgy, agriculture, food security, sustainable energy, transport and logistics, as well as certification and international standardisation.
The second day, "Drivers of the New Economy", turns to fast-growing fields such as financial infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, advanced healthcare and wellness, the platform economy and real estate.
Hospitality, tourism and the sports economy will also be on the agenda.
Russian participants include Sber, Alfa-Bank, VTB, VEB.RF, the Russian Export Center, Roscongress, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the Russian Federation, Delovaya Rossiya, R-Pharm, Fesco, Abrau-Durso and AFK Sistema, as well as the governments of Moscow and the Krasnodar Territory.
They will meet Thai counterparts, including the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) Office, the Federation of Thai Industries, CP Group, EGAT, the Thai Chamber of Commerce and Board of Trade, Central Group, Minor International, Dusit Thani, BDMS, Thai Union, Supalai and the Digital Council of Thailand.
Ivan Demchenko, chairman of the RTBC, said he was convinced the potential for closer relations was "enormous".
"Today, mutually beneficial cooperation between our countries spans a wide range of sectors, from traditional trade and tourism to technological innovation," he said. "The primary objective of the forum is to strengthen active business partnerships and open up new market niches for entrepreneurs in both countries."
Alongside the main sessions, the forum will feature "Days of Moscow in Bangkok" and the debut of an official "Made in Russia" trade pavilion.
Intended as a permanent platform for bilateral trade, it will showcase Russian exports ranging from food products and pharmaceuticals to industrial machinery and IT solutions.
Vladimir Kovalev, the RTBC's executive director, said the pavilion would give Russian manufacturers comprehensive help in entering the Thai market.
"Exporters will gain access to a modern B2B platform, complete with assistance in certification, legal guidance, and marketing support," he said, adding that the initiative was expected to produce "a substantial increase in bilateral trade turnover".
Beyond the boardroom, the programme includes a lively cultural and sporting line-up. Lumpini Park will host the "MIR" Russian-Thai Cultural Festival, and a theatrical performance, Thai Dictionary, will star Russian actress Irina Starshenbaum alongside Thai actor and model Sean Tsindahot.
On 29 October, junior ice hockey teams from Russia and Thailand will play a friendly match. A masterclass will be led by Roman Rotenberg, first vice-president of the Russian Ice Hockey Federation and head coach of the Russia-25 team, and top Russian figure skaters will give exhibition performances.
On 31 October, business executives and professional athletes from both countries will take part in a friendly badminton tournament.
Business representatives, investors and members of the press are invited to attend and are encouraged to register early to secure access to the business and networking sessions.
The deadline is 26 October. Registration: https://forum.rusthaibusiness.com/en/rtif-main.html#registration

articles.title: Taiwan Brings 200+ Automotive Suppliers to AAPEX 2026 as U.S. Buyers Seek Resilient, Diversified Supply Chains - The Manila Times
articles.summary: Taiwan Brings 200+ Automotive Suppliers to AAPEX 2026 as U.S. Buyers Seek Resilient, Diversified Supply Chains  The Manila Times
articles.full_text:
From 360-degree camera systems to heavy-duty suspension, Taiwan Flagship Showcase puts next-generation aftermarket products in front of buyers, November 3-5
LAS VEGAS, Oct. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As U.S. buyers work to build more resilient and diversified supply chains, more than 200 Taiwanese suppliers will bring their capabilities to AAPEX 2026, November 3-5 at the Venetian Expo in Las Vegas. As part of Taiwan’s broader presence at AAPEX, and under the TEAM TAIWAN brand, the Taiwan Flagship Showcase will give distributors, retailers, and industry partners direct access to Taiwanese manufacturers across six categories: auto parts, accessories, body parts, electrical and electronics, lighting, tools, and equipment.
Presented by Taiwan International Trade Administration (TITA), Ministry of Economic Affairs, and Taiwan External Trade Development Council (TAITRA), Taiwan Flagship Showcase features the strength of Taiwanese industrial supply chains to global buyers. Located at Booth V19622, this showcase brings Taiwan’s precision engineering and automotive electronics capabilities into focus through an Industry Scenario Zone, Digital Kiosk Zone, and onstage presentations.
The U.S. aftermarket is expected to reach $599.7 billion in 2026, according to the AAPEX 2026 media guide, and Taiwan is an established partner in it. The United States is Taiwan's largest market, accounting for roughly 50% of shipments in 2025, mainly headlight, body, and collision parts. Taiwan holds up to 85% of the global collision parts market, according to the Industrial Economics and Knowledge Center (IEK).
Many Taiwanese suppliers also hold the certifications highly valued by the U.S. automotive aftermarket, including ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 for quality management, and CAPA certification, which U.S. insurers recognize for collision repair parts.
What buyers will see
Taiwan Flagship Showcase spans both sides of the aftermarket: technology and maintenance.
On the technology side, buyers can explore 360-degree cameras and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) for vehicle visibility and safety, along with sensors and automotive electronics. Industrial video scopes and imaging devices support inspection and diagnostics.
On the maintenance side, products such as suspension and steering components, brake linings, and professional lubrication equipment are essential for aftermarket business. Lighting and styling accessories round out the range, giving distributors and repair shops the opportunity to explore products across multiple aftermarket categories.
The showcase launches on November 3 with an Opening Ceremony. Offering a relaxing evening of Taiwanese hospitality, Taiwan Night gives suppliers, buyers, and industry stakeholders a chance to build relationships beyond the show floor.
On November 4 and 5, customized procurement meetings will connect buyers with Taiwanese suppliers to explore sourcing opportunities. Throughout the exhibition, Pitch & Demo Shows will bring Taiwanese exhibitors and industry experts together to present products and technologies for automotive aftermarket applications, including electronics, lighting, body parts, repair tools, and equipment. "Trends to Watch” session on the final day of the show, an industry expert will be invited to share insights into the US aftermarket trends.
Buyers, industry partners, and media are invited to RSVP for the Opening Ceremony and guided tour, Pitch & Demo sessions, and Taiwan Night using the event-specific registration links below. articles.title: Malaysia posts RM1.57tril exports in nine months, but growth may cool - KLSE Screener
articles.summary: Malaysia posts RM1.57tril exports in nine months, but growth may cool  KLSE Screener
articles.full_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's exports hit a record RM1.57 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, but an economist cautions that the headline growth figures alone do not reveal the underlying strength of the country's trade performance.
Exports rose 34 per cent year-on-year, supported by strong electrical and electronics (E&E) shipments and expanding demand in non-traditional markets.
However, Putra Business School professor Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said more detailed data were needed to determine how much of the increase came from higher shipment volumes, prices or a shift towards higher-value products.
"We still need to look at the detailed volume and unit-value data to distinguish these effects and assess the underlying strength of export performance," he told Business Times.
Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade) today said total trade grew 30.1 per cent to RM2.91 trillion during the period, while imports increased 25.7 per cent to RM1.34 trillion.
This resulted in a trade surplus of RM232.38 billion.
E&E products remained the main export driver, contributing an increase of RM253.88 billion amid global demand linked to artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology adoption.
Other contributors included petroleum products, optical and scientific equipment, machinery, equipment and parts, as well as liquefied natural gas.
Downstream palm oil-based manufactured products, particularly oleochemicals, also recorded double-digit export growth.
Meanwhile, automotive parts and accessories, pharmaceutical products, metal furniture and aerospace products posted positive growth.
These industries also feature significant participation from Malaysian small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Ahmed Razman expects export growth to moderate in 2027 as global demand normalises and the high base of comparison makes further gains harder to achieve.
He said Malaysia could maintain a positive export trajectory if semiconductor demand, AI-related investment and E&E production remained strong.
However, weaker global economic growth, geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions could weigh on the outlook.
Economist Dr Geoffrey Williams expects the strong performance to continue into 2027, citing sustained external demand, higher export prices and increased volumes.
"The strong export demand is further evidence that the standard narrative of global headwinds, Middle East conflict and Trump tariffs is false," Williams said.
AI Demand Drives E&E Exports
The E&E sector remained a major contributor to export growth with exports increasing by RM253.88 billion amid strong global demand linked to AI.
Ahmed Razman said Malaysia's reliance on the semiconductor and AI investment cycle could expose exports to a slowdown in technology spending.
"Sustained investment in AI infrastructure, data centres and advanced computing supports demand for Malaysian electronics," he said.
However, weaker semiconductor demand or a slowdown in technology investment could significantly affect exports, he added.
Ahmed Razman said Malaysia should move towards higher-value semiconductor activities while diversifying its manufacturing base.
Williams identified technology, AI and semiconductors as key drivers alongside traditional sectors such as oil and gas and palm oil.
Beyond E&E, Matrade said petroleum products, optical and scientific equipment, machinery, equipment and parts as well as liquefied natural gas, were contributors to export growth.
Exports of downstream palm oil-based manufactured products, particularly oleochemicals, also recorded double-digit growth.
Other products recording positive growth included automotive parts and accessories, pharmaceutical products, metal furniture and aerospace products, which feature substantial participation from Malaysian SMEs.
Higher Imports Reflect Stronger Activity
The 25.7 per cent increase in imports could indicate stronger manufacturing activity and investment although their composition needs further examination.
Ahmed Razman said the increase suggested stronger demand for intermediate inputs, machinery and capital equipment.
"It also reflects Malaysia's deep integration into global supply chains, where imported components are processed or assembled before being exported," he added.
However, he said imports should be assessed by category to distinguish productive investment from consumption and inventory accumulation.
Williams said imports reflected stronger domestic activity including goods brought into Malaysia for re-export and purchases by consumers.
Market Diversification Continues
Exports to non-traditional markets across Africa, Central Asia, South Asia and Latin America rose 21.5 per cent to RM136.36 billion in the first nine months of 2026.
Exports to Namibia surged 426.1 per cent, while shipments to South Africa increased 101 per cent, Libya 79.3 per cent, Angola 55.6 per cent and Brazil 41 per cent.
Ahmed Razman said the growth was encouraging but insufficient to substantially reduce Malaysia's reliance on established trading partners.
He said Malaysia should expand market access through trade agreements, stronger business networks and targeted export promotion.
"Crucially, diversification must involve a broader range of products and industries, not simply more destinations for the same exports," he said.
Williams said expanding into non-traditional markets would gradually reduce Malaysia's reliance on established trading partners.
Malaysia's free trade agreement (FTA) partners accounted for RM986.38 billion or 62.8 per cent of total exports with shipments to these markets growing 25.8 per cent.
Exports to 21 of Malaysia's 24 FTA partners increased, led by Mexico at 52.1 per cent, Vietnam at 44.9 per cent, the United Kingdom at 41.1 per cent and Thailand at 32.3 per cent.

articles.title: Bismuth Telluride Nanowires Market Forecast to 2035, Driven by Waste Heat Recovery Demand - IndexBox
articles.summary: Bismuth Telluride Nanowires Market Forecast to 2035, Driven by Waste Heat Recovery Demand  IndexBox
articles.full_text:
American Elements
Major supplier of bismuth telluride nanowires
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Bismuth Telluride Nanowires market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global market for bismuth telluride (Bi₂Te₃) nanowires stands at the intersection of advanced materials science and next-generation energy technologies. As of 2026, this specialized nanomaterial is transitioning from laboratory-scale synthesis to early commercial deployment, propelled by its exceptional thermoelectric performance at the nanoscale. The market remains modest in volume but carries high strategic value, enabling precision cooling, waste heat recovery, and micro-power generation in applications ranging from consumer electronics to medical diagnostics.
Demand is concentrated in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, where semiconductor and thermoelectric device manufacturers are investing in nanowire-enhanced modules. The supply chain is fragmented, involving specialized chemical synthesizers, nanotechnology developers, and integrated device manufacturers. Key challenges include scalable, cost-effective production and seamless integration into final devices. The forecast horizon 2026–2035 anticipates a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14.2%, with the market index rising to 378 by 2035 (2025=100).
Growth will be driven by tightening energy-efficiency regulations, miniaturization of electronics, and the push for solid-state cooling and energy harvesting. This report provides a data-driven view of market dynamics, competitive intelligence, and strategic implications for stakeholders across the value chain.
The baseline scenario for the global bismuth telluride nanowires market projects robust expansion from 2026 to 2035, with a CAGR of 14.2% and a market index reaching 378 by 2035 (2025=100). This outlook assumes continued technological maturation, gradual cost reductions in nanowire synthesis, and accelerating adoption in thermoelectric cooling and waste heat recovery. Volume growth will be led by the electronics and automotive sectors, where thermal management and energy efficiency are critical.
The market will remain supply-constrained in the near term due to limited production capacity and complex synthesis methods, but capacity expansions and process innovations are expected to alleviate bottlenecks by the late 2020s. Pricing will remain premium, reflecting high R&D costs and specialized inputs, though economies of scale will moderate price declines. Geographically, Asia-Pacific will dominate consumption, supported by semiconductor manufacturing hubs, while North America and Europe will drive innovation and high-value applications. Regulatory support for energy-efficient technologies and the phase-down of traditional refrigerants will provide tailwinds.
Key risks include competition from alternative thermoelectric materials, volatility in bismuth and tellurium supply, and slower-than-expected integration into end devices. Overall, the market is poised for transformative growth, with cumulative investment in nanowire-based thermoelectric solutions expected to reshape the competitive landscape.
Thermoelectric cooling modules represent the largest end-use sector for bismuth telluride nanowires, accounting for approximately 32% of market share in 2026. These modules are increasingly adopted for precision cooling of laser diodes, infrared sensors, and electronic components where conventional refrigeration is impractical. The demand is driven by the need for compact, reliable, and vibration-free cooling solutions. Through 2035, the sector will benefit from the miniaturization of electronics and the proliferation of high-power-density devices. Nanowire-enhanced modules offer higher cooling efficiency and faster response times compared to bulk materials, making them ideal for thermal management in data centers and consumer electronics.
Key demand indicators include the growth of 5G infrastructure, the expansion of electric vehicles (EVs) with battery thermal management needs, and the rising complexity of medical diagnostic equipment. However, adoption is tempered by cost and the availability of alternative cooling technologies. The trend toward higher integration and the development of flexible thermoelectric modules will open new opportunities, particularly in wearable electronics and portable medical devices. Current trend: Growing demand for solid-state cooling in electronics, medical devices, and automotive.
Major trends: Shift toward solid-state cooling in consumer electronics, Integration of thermoelectric modules in EV battery thermal management, Development of flexible and conformable cooling modules, and Increasing use in medical diagnostics for precise temperature control.
Representative participants: Ferrotec Corporation, Laird Thermal Systems, II-VI Incorporated, KELK Ltd, and Thermo Fisher Scientific.
Waste heat recovery systems are the second-largest application, with a 28% share in 2026, and are expected to witness the fastest growth through 2035. Bismuth telluride nanowires enable thermoelectric generators (TEGs) to convert waste heat from automotive exhausts, industrial furnaces, and power plants into electricity. The demand is propelled by stringent emission regulations and corporate sustainability targets. In the automotive sector, TEGs are being developed to recover heat from exhaust systems, reducing fuel consumption and CO2 emissions. Industrial applications focus on recovering heat from high-temperature processes, where nanowire-based TEGs offer higher conversion efficiency than bulk materials.
The sector's growth is supported by government incentives for energy-efficient technologies and the increasing cost of energy. Key demand-side indicators include the production volume of hybrid and electric vehicles, the implementation of carbon pricing mechanisms, and the adoption of industrial energy management systems. Challenges include the high cost of nanowire synthesis and the need for durable, high-temperature-resistant materials. Nevertheless, ongoing R&D and pilot projects are expected to drive commercialization, with significant uptake anticipated in the late 2020s and beyond. Current trend: Accelerating adoption in automotive and industrial processes to improve energy efficiency.
Major trends: Automotive TEG integration for exhaust heat recovery, Industrial waste heat recovery in steel and cement plants, Development of high-temperature nanowire composites, and Government subsidies for energy efficiency projects.
Representative participants: Materion Corporation, Umicore, 5N Plus, Evident Technologies, and American Elements.
Precision temperature control accounts for 18% of the market in 2026, serving applications that require exact thermal stability, such as laboratory instruments, semiconductor lithography, and analytical equipment. Bismuth telluride nanowires enable compact, high-precision thermoelectric coolers that can maintain temperatures within ±0.01°C. The demand is driven by the expansion of R&D activities in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and materials science, as well as the growth of semiconductor manufacturing in Asia-Pacific. Through 2035, the sector will benefit from the increasing automation of laboratories and the miniaturization of analytical devices.
Key demand indicators include R&D spending in life sciences, the number of semiconductor fabrication plants, and the adoption of point-of-care diagnostic devices. The trend toward lab-on-a-chip and microfluidic systems will create new opportunities for nanowire-based cooling. However, the high cost of nanowires and the availability of alternative cooling methods (e.g., Peltier devices using bulk materials) may limit adoption in price-sensitive segments. Nevertheless, the need for higher precision and reliability in critical applications will sustain demand for nanowire-enhanced solutions. Current trend: Steady growth in laboratory equipment, analytical instruments, and semiconductor manufacturing.
Major trends: Miniaturization of analytical instruments, Integration of thermoelectric coolers in lab-on-a-chip devices, Demand for high-precision temperature control in semiconductor manufacturing, and Growth of point-of-care diagnostics.
Representative participants: Thermo Fisher Scientific, Nanostructured & Amorphous Materials, Inc, Alfa Aesar, KELK Ltd, and Ferrotec Corporation.
Infrared sensors represent 12% of the market in 2026, utilizing bismuth telluride nanowires for uncooled thermal detectors and gas sensors. The demand is driven by the growing adoption of thermal imaging in surveillance, automotive night vision, and building diagnostics, as well as the need for sensitive gas sensors in environmental monitoring and industrial safety. Nanowire-based sensors offer higher sensitivity and faster response times compared to conventional thermopiles. Through 2035, the sector will expand with the proliferation of IoT devices and smart sensors, particularly in smart homes and industrial IoT.
Key demand indicators include the production of thermal cameras, the deployment of gas sensor networks, and defense spending on infrared technology. The trend toward multispectral and hyperspectral imaging will create demand for advanced nanowire architectures. Challenges include the need for consistent nanowire quality and integration with readout electronics. However, ongoing R&D in nanowire synthesis and device fabrication is expected to overcome these barriers, enabling broader adoption. Current trend: Increasing use in thermal imaging, gas sensing, and defense applications.
Major trends: Growth of thermal imaging in automotive and security, Miniaturization of gas sensors for IoT, Advancements in multispectral infrared detectors, and Defense modernization programs.

Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Respiratory Protection market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global respiratory protection equipment (RPE) market is entering a phase of steady expansion, with demand projected to accelerate through 2035. This analytical overview, based on the 2026 edition of IndexBox research, examines the structural forces shaping the industry, from regulatory tightening to shifting industrial geography. The market encompasses disposable filtering facepiece respirators, reusable half-mask and full-face respirators, powered air-purifying respirators (PAPR), self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), escape hoods, and replacement filters and cartridges.
Growth is anchored in the essential nature of respiratory protection across healthcare, manufacturing, construction, mining, emergency services, and defense. While mature markets in North America and Europe exhibit replacement-driven demand, emerging economies in Asia-Pacific and Latin America are witnessing accelerated adoption as occupational safety standards converge with industrial output. The competitive landscape remains fragmented, featuring multinational corporations with broad portfolios alongside specialized manufacturers. Technological integration, supply chain localization, and persistent awareness of airborne hazards are set to define the market's trajectory to 2035.
This report provides a data-driven view of market size, segmentation, trade flows, and competitive dynamics for stakeholders across the value chain.
The baseline scenario for the world respiratory protection market anticipates moderate but sustained growth over the 2026-2035 forecast period, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.8% and a market index reaching 176 by 2035 (2025=100). This outlook assumes continued enforcement of occupational safety regulations, gradual expansion of industrial activity in emerging markets, and a stable replacement cycle for consumable components such as filters and cartridges.
The market's essential nature provides a floor for demand, while upside potential stems from tightening regulatory frameworks in Asia-Pacific and Latin America, where safety standards are progressively aligning with those of developed regions. Downside risks include economic slowdowns that could delay industrial capex and discretionary spending on premium RPE, as well as potential supply chain disruptions for specialized filter media. The product mix is expected to shift gradually toward reusable and powered systems in industrial settings, while disposable masks retain a dominant volume share in healthcare and general public use.
Pricing dynamics will be influenced by raw material costs for filter media and elastomers, alongside certification and testing expenses. Overall, the market is poised for steady expansion, with technological integration and supply chain localization as key strategic themes.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
- Tightening occupational safety and health regulations globally, particularly in emerging industrial economies, compel employers to adopt certified respiratory protection.
- Rising industrial activity in manufacturing, construction, and mining sectors increases the number of workers exposed to airborne hazards, directly boosting RPE demand.
- Persistent awareness of airborne biological threats following recent pandemics sustains demand for disposable masks and high-filtration respirators in healthcare and public settings.
- Expansion of healthcare infrastructure and infection control protocols in developing regions drives procurement of N95 and FFP2-grade disposable respirators.
- Growth in emergency services and military spending on CBRN preparedness supports demand for SCBA, escape hoods, and advanced filtration systems.
- Technological advancements in smart PPE and connected safety solutions encourage replacement and upgrade cycles in developed markets.
Potential Growth Constraints
- High costs associated with certification, testing, and compliance for advanced respirators can limit adoption among small and medium-sized enterprises.
- Economic downturns and industrial capex cuts may delay non-essential purchases and extend replacement cycles for reusable equipment.
- Supply chain vulnerabilities for specialized filter media and components can constrain production and increase lead times.
- Competition from low-cost, uncertified products in some emerging markets undermines pricing and compliance with safety standards.
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
End-Use Industry Demand Split (%)
Healthcare and Medical (estimated share: 29%)
The healthcare and medical segment represents a cornerstone of respiratory protection demand, driven by the need to safeguard workers against airborne pathogens, hazardous drugs, and particulate matter. Hospitals, clinics, and long-term care facilities maintain stringent infection control protocols that mandate the use of disposable filtering facepiece respirators (N95, FFP2) and, in specialized settings, powered air-purifying respirators (PAPR) for high-risk procedures. The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the criticality of stockpiling and supply chain resilience, leading to increased government stockpiles and long-term procurement contracts.
Through 2035, demand will be supported by aging populations in developed regions, expanding healthcare infrastructure in emerging markets, and persistent awareness of airborne biological threats. Key demand-side indicators include healthcare spending as a share of GDP, hospital admission rates, and regulatory updates on occupational safety for healthcare workers. The shift toward reusable respirators in some settings may temper volume growth for disposables, but overall value growth is expected to remain robust as facilities upgrade to higher-filtration and more comfortable designs. Current trend: Stable growth supported by infection control protocols and aging populations.
Major trends: Increased stockpiling and government procurement of N95 and FFP2 respirators, Adoption of PAPR systems for high-risk aerosol-generating procedures, Rising demand for comfortable, breathable designs for long shifts, and Integration of antimicrobial treatments in disposable masks.
Representative participants: 3M, Honeywell International, Kimberly-Clark, Ansell, and Alpha Pro Tech.
Industrial and Manufacturing (estimated share: 25%)
The industrial and manufacturing segment is a major consumer of respiratory protection, encompassing sectors such as chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food processing, and metalworking. Workers are exposed to a wide range of airborne hazards, including dust, fumes, vapors, and gases, necessitating the use of reusable half-mask and full-face respirators with appropriate filter cartridges, as well as disposable masks for particulate protection. Demand is closely tied to industrial production levels, employment in manufacturing, and the enforcement of occupational safety regulations.
Through 2035, growth will be supported by the expansion of manufacturing activities in Asia-Pacific and Latin America, where safety standards are progressively tightening. The shift toward reusable respirators and PAPR systems in high-hazard environments is expected to drive value growth, while disposable masks remain prevalent for lower-risk tasks. Key demand-side indicators include manufacturing value added, industrial employment, and regulatory compliance spending. Technological advancements, such as connected safety devices that monitor filter life and exposure levels, are anticipated to gain traction, encouraging replacement and upgrade cycles.
Current trend: Moderate growth driven by occupational hazard regulations and industrial output.
Major trends: Tightening occupational exposure limits for airborne contaminants, Adoption of connected safety solutions for real-time monitoring, Shift toward reusable respirators to reduce long-term costs, and Growth in pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturing in emerging markets.
Representative participants: 3M, Honeywell International, MSA Safety, Drägerwerk, and Moldex-Metric.
Construction and Mining (estimated share: 21%)
Construction and mining operations generate significant airborne hazards, including silica dust, asbestos fibers, welding fumes, and diesel particulate matter. Respiratory protection is mandatory in these sectors, with demand spanning disposable particulate respirators, reusable half-mask respirators, and powered air-purifying respirators (PAPR) for high-exposure tasks. The segment's demand is closely linked to construction spending, mining output, and the enforcement of health and safety regulations, such as OSHA's silica standard in the United States.
Through 2035, growth will be driven by infrastructure development in emerging economies, particularly in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, and by increasing awareness of occupational lung diseases. The adoption of PAPR systems is expected to rise in mining and heavy construction due to their superior protection and comfort. Key demand-side indicators include construction value added, mining production volumes, and regulatory compliance rates. Challenges include the seasonal nature of construction activity and the prevalence of informal employment in some regions, which can hinder consistent RPE use. Current trend: Steady growth underpinned by dust and silica regulations.
Major trends: Stricter enforcement of silica dust regulations, Growing adoption of PAPR systems in mining for comfort and protection, Increased infrastructure spending in emerging economies, and Rising awareness of occupational lung diseases.
Representative participants: 3M, MSA Safety, Honeywell International, Bullard, and Sundström Safety.
